Everyone has some point in their life when they finally realize that they aren't a kid anymore and they have to accept that they have grown up. When did it happen to you?
When did you realize that you were actually an adult?

I'm not sure it's even really hit me completely. There's been points in my life that definitely stick as points where I thought "Yes this is it!" Only to realise at the next life changing moment that I was wrong.

Moving to university, moving into my first flat living on my own, the day I first met my step son, setting up my pension, my first job that paid over £20,000, halfway down the wedding aisle, sitting down with my husband discussing if we should start trying for a baby..... All those things made me feel incredibly grown up at the time but really I'm still just an idiotic kid that doesn't really know what I'm doing each day!

I'm hoping that I'm the norm and that most people are sort of muddling their way through life as best they can. I'm not sure I'll ever 100% feel like an adult.

Edit: spelling

I still feel like "the kid" a lot of the time even though I'm pushing thirty. I don't have kids, I'm not married, I spend my free time gaming - I wouldn't trade it for the alternative, but it does feel sometimes like all the folks that did make that trade have definite thoughts about my decision not to do so. I think, realistically, the point at which you start "acting old" is that point where you have a family and you're placing your family's needs and future ahead of yours personally. Most of the behaviors that I associate with older folks are the ones that are centered around being mature enough to sacrifice your personal time in service of your family.

I find it commendable, I just don't feel like doing it at the moment.

Moving out to live on my own with my girlfriend - I had already lived away from home for a year but moving in with her made it sink home that I actually have responsibilities like rent that someone partially relies on me for.
Late twenties, live on my own, across the country from my family. Have a full time job engineering. I still feel 12.

Taking care of my sister during a mental episode and arguing with asshole hospital doctors that dont take her serious and prescribed her medication that could have killed her, because they didn't even bother to read her chart.
When you have to start thinking about pensions and mortgagees just seems weird

A few weeks after moving away from my parents to go live in a college dormitory. I realized that I couldn't just tell my parents to buy me what I need anymore; I had to go and buy food, supplies, and amenities for myself.
when I got excited to get socks and boxers for christmas.
I don't feel like an adult now and I'm 42. I do, however, feel old as shit.

After I had gone through puberty and stopped growing taller.

As for being "grown up" mentally, I don't know if the day will ever come, or what it even means. I've had to stand on my own feet for a while, and I still feel like a kid sometimes.

When I started waking up on the love seat at 3 am because I fell asleep there at 10 on a Saturday. Then I spend all day Sunday wishing I didn't fall asleep there because my back hurts.
